newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks look to open softer, watching bonds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks look to open softer, watching bonds.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open slightly lower on Tuesday, after the benchmark 30-year Treasury broke through a critical seven percent yield and pushed the stock futures index down.
"Bonds are giving up ground right now and that usually hits stocks," Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said.

The long bond was trading off 14/32 at a 7.02 percent yield, compared with Friday's yield of 6.99 percent. Analysts have said that when bond yields touch seven percent, money managers shift funds from stocks to bonds and cash.
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index, which had been positive earlier on Tuesday, slipped to trade off 4.25 points at 843.50.
Stocks and nervous bonds would look to economic data due out Tuesday morning for direction, analysts said.

Consumer confidence for May will be released at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT and was forecast at 118.1 versus 116.8. Existing homes data for April, also due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, were forecast at 4.09 million compared with 4.11 million.
Telecommunications stocks were expected to be active, on reports that AT&T Corp was in merger talks.
